verdict.rationale: Solid's first-party docs say components are plain functions that set up their own reactive state (signals via an accessor/setter, plus derived state), with JSX, fragments, Context and Stores for composition. Hands-on reports of porting react-bootstrap and running a largish product corroborate building complex component-based UIs. Users note that props must stay reactive (no destructuring, values passed as accessors), which is a rough edge rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of component composition and prop-passing patterns, and smoother props reactivity ergonomics.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build encapsulated components that manage their own local state and compose them into complex UIs

citations.quote: In Solid, components are just functions - rendering is determined purely by how your state is used - so you're free to organize your code how you like
your components are regular JavaScript functions that run once to set up your view
Create a piece of reactive state, giving us an accessor, count(), and a setter, setCount()
Performant state management is built-in with Context and Stores
Provides modern framework features like JSX, fragments, Context, Portals, Suspense
